title: MeHyper: Accelerating Hypergraph Neural Networks by Exploring Implicit Dataflows
problem: Hypergraph Neural Networks (HGNNs) based on hyperedge-centric dataflow independently process vertex and hyperedge aggregation tasks, causing significant computational redundancy from recalculating shared information (intermediate feature values) across these tasks.
motivation: HGNNs are increasingly used for complex relational data analysis, but their computational redundancy and large volumes of intermediate features create memory bandwidth bottlenecks that make existing CPU/GPU systems highly inefficient.
method: MeHyper introduces a microedge concept that captures fine-grained shared information between aggregation tasks, replacing the hyperedge-centric model with a microedge-centric dataflow that processes shared information once and distributes it to all dependent tasks. The execution follows a Read-Process-Activate-Generate model optimized for parallel microedge task processing. The hardware accelerator features a decoupled pipeline for improved computational parallelism and a hierarchical feature management strategy that partitions on-chip memory across feature granularities to reduce off-chip DRAM accesses for the large intermediate feature vectors generated during microedge aggregation.
key_novelty: First identification and exploitation of implicit dataflow dependencies within HGNNs via the microedge abstraction, eliminating inter-task computational redundancy across vertex and hyperedge aggregation.
contributions: Discovery and formalization of implicit dataflows in HGNNs via the microedge concept
Microedge-centric dataflow model with Read-Process-Activate-Generate execution for parallel processing
Decoupled pipeline architecture for maximizing computational parallelism in HGNN acceleration
Hierarchical on-chip feature management reducing off-chip accesses; 1032x/10.51x speedup over PyG-CPU/HyperGef

metrics.energy_or_tops_w: 1169.03x energy efficiency over PyG-CPU; 9.96x over HyperGef

limitations: Evaluation is limited to HGNN workloads; applicability to standard GNNs or heterogeneous graph models is not assessed.
primary_theme: Microedge-centric dataflow accelerator for redundancy-free HGNN computation
